output:
**One star for now: our migration is still unresolved**

I’m the director of Bridger Bend Community Library, a one-branch library near Bozeman, Montana, with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. We went live on October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped out—approximately 640 holds gone. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, each saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” We still do not have a resolution.

During sales, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we received was a shared inbox. For a library our size, that difference matters. We do not have an IT department to take over when a migration goes wrong.

The consequences are not just administrative. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect the large-print Westerns he had on hold. We had no record of his hold and sent him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been recording checkouts on index cards. Our staff and patrons are carrying the burden of a service we are paying to use.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demonstration, and the staff interface is better than our old system. My concern is not the product idea. It is the support when essential functions fail.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and our library’s line item is on the agenda. I need to be able to explain what is being done, by whom, and on what timetable.

I am asking someone senior at Stackhouse to call me this week, identify a named person responsible for our case, and provide a concrete recovery plan for circulation and the missing holds.

For other small-library directors: get support response times and migration staffing commitments in writing before signing. Ask what happens when circulation stops working.

One star for now. I will revisit this review if Stackhouse fixes these problems and follows through on support.
